dct_description_sm: This multi-year project aimed to examine the vulnerabilities to climate change and adaptive capacities of Yukon tree species and forest ecosystems, in order to project future forest scenarios and forest management practices. Information collected over the course of this project is significant in terms of future decision-making and long-term climate change effects on forest management, as well as in terms of increasing adaptive capacity by raising awareness of tree species vulnerabilities to climate change. During its first year, focus was placed on planning. The following objectives were set for 2008-2009: (1) to identify partners (university partners, i.e. the University of Northern British Columbia's (UNBC) Ecosystem Science and Management Program; (2) to determine and report on the state-of-knowledge on the vulnerability and adaptive capacity of eight Yukon tree species, as well as forest management responses; and (3) to develop research questions and methodology for the project's second and third years.   In the second year of the project, a focus was placed on initiation of research and analysis. The following objectives were outlined: to communicate and disseminate the results of the Vulnerability and Adaptive Capacity of Yukon Tree Species to Climate Change report (completed in Year 1); (2) to establish a baseline of information about site conditions, tree distributions and growth in the Teslin and Dawson forest districts; (3) to describe species-specific tree responses to climate and other primary environmental factors under different site conditions in Yukon; and (4) to develop a framework and methodology for incorporating climate change adaptation considerations.  In the third year, the project aimed: (1) to examine the responses of Yukon tree species to changes in climate factors; (2) to inform the government and policy-makers of the observed responses and vulnerabilities to develop adaptation policy and sustainable forest management practices. (3) to aid in the development of research and adaptation priorities through case studies of community involvement. In doing so, an improved capacity of communities to implement adaptation strategies will be achieved.

dct_title_s: Assessing the Vulnerability to Climate Change and Adaptive Capacity of Yukon Forest Tree Species and Ecosystems
